notifications.explainer: Link your own Teams chat to receive the alerts routed to you. Unlink at any time to stop them.
notifications.managed: Your IT department sends messages to your Teams chat through Teamster, so it cannot be unlinked here. Signing in connects it to your account, so the alerts routed to you arrive there too.
notifications.unlink_managed: Your IT department manages this chat, so it cannot be unlinked.

palette.conditional_help: A block that renders for an open event and another for a closed one.
palette.facts_help: Label and value pairs, which is what most cards are.
palette.labels_help: Every label the event carries. The inner toJSON builds the text, the outer one quotes it.
palette.link_help: An action that opens a runbook or a dashboard.
palette.starter_help: Replace the card with a complete example to edit down
palette.text_help: A line of text, wrapped. toJSON quotes it, so a value containing a quotation mark is safe.
permissions.channels_failed: Channels could not be listed for this Team.
permissions.explainer: Tick what this role may reach. A role with nothing ticked reaches every Team and channel, which is how an installation behaves before anyone narrows it.
permissions.heading: Which Teams and channels may a role deliver to?
permissions.load_failed: Microsoft Graph did not answer, so there is nothing to tick. Permissions can still be set through the API.
permissions.no_admin: Admins are not listed: they reach everything by definition, so a scope set for them would be stored and then ignored.
permissions.unrestricted_note: Ticking a whole Team grants its channels, including ones added later. Ticking channels individually grants only those.
picker.channel_needs_team: Choose a Team first; its channels appear here.
preview.json_note: The tenant and channel IDs are placeholders; everything else is sent as shown.
recipients.blocked_detail: Blocked since {1}: {0}. This does not stop the next alert from trying again -- a successful delivery clears it automatically.
recipients.empty: Nobody has linked a chat yet. A person does this themselves, from the admin UI, once they hold at least the viewer role.
recipients.explainer: Everybody who has linked their Teams chat to receive alerts directly. Unlinking removes the binding; a route still pointing at them shows up as a missing recipient in the routing picture.
recipients.heading: Recipients
recipients.no_routes: no routes deliver to this person
routes.badge_both: channel and person — edit to choose one
routes.empty: No routes yet. Every message goes to the global default destination.
routes.global_default_hint: Catches every message no route claims, the default route included. Its destination is changed under Destinations.
routes.greedy: Deliver instead of the route it refines, not as well as it
routes.parent_none: — nothing, this is a root route —
routes.target_hint: A route delivers to one channel or one person; a root route must choose one. A refining route that inherits its target must use a different template. You can only choose your own chat as the person.
routes.template_none: — none, send the message's own title/text/card —
routing.graph_help: Arrows follow an alert from the webhook it arrived at through the routes that match it to the channels it lands in. A route whose selector pins teamster_source is reached from that webhook only. A dashed arrow is a child route refining its parent, labelled with whether it delivers as well as its parent or instead of it. A dotted arrow is a Teams V2 endpoint posting straight to its channel, without routing. Check a label set to highlight every path it takes. Drag a node to rearrange it, scroll to zoom.
routing.match_heading: Which routes would a message take?
routing.templates_heading: Which routes render with which template?
routing.templates_help: Rendering is not a step an alert takes, so it has its own picture. A template with no route beside it is used by nothing.
teams.directory_error: Microsoft Graph could not list the Teams, so only teams that destinations use are shown: {0}
teams.explainer: The bot posts to a channel only in a team where its Teams app is installed. Teams that destinations use but that lack the app come first.
teams.heading: Where the Teams app is installed
teams.how_add: An owner of the team opens the app in Teams, chooses Add to a team and picks any channel.
teams.how_catalog: A Teams admin publishes the app to the organization's catalog once (see manifest/README.md).
teams.how_event: The bot hears about it and the team moves to Installed here. Removing the app moves it back.
teams.how_heading: Installing the app in a team
teams.installed_empty: The app is not known to be installed in any team yet.
teams.needs_app: Used by destinations, app not confirmed
teams.needs_app_empty: Every team a destination uses has the app.
teams.no_bot: The bot is not configured, so no channel receives anything. Set the bot credentials first.
teams.unknown_note: Without the Graph permission TeamsAppInstallation.ReadForTeam.All, a team that installed the app before Teamster started listening shows as unknown until it sends the bot anything.
templates.empty: No templates yet. A route needs one to render its message.
templates.name: Name
templates.preset_confirm: Replace the title, text and card with the preset?
templates.preset_help: Fill the form with a complete template written for one webhook
templates.source_defaults_hint: Renders every message from that webhook whose route or endpoint names no template that handles it.
templates.sources_hint: Leave all unticked for any webhook. Pickers offer the template only where it applies, and an alert from another webhook gets the built-in message.
timezone.label: Time zone
tokens.config_token: The token in webhook.token is accepted as well. It is not listed here.
tokens.explainer: An access token admits a sender to /webhook/alertmanager and /webhook/universal. Senders pass it as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Give each sender its own, so one can be revoked without breaking the others.
tokens.heading: Webhook access tokens
tokens.name: Name
tokens.new_token: Copy the token for {0} now. It is stored only as a digest and cannot be shown again.
userinfo.heading: User info
userinfo.name: Name
userinfo.sign_in_again: This session started before Teamster kept what the identity provider sent. Sign out and in again to see scopes, groups and the role claim.
userinfo.subject: Subject
webhooks.empty: No Teams V2 webhooks yet. Add one to give a sender a URL it can post its existing payload to.
webhooks.hint: Lower case letters, digits and hyphens. The URL becomes /teamsv2/<team>/<channel>/<token>, and the token is shown once when it is generated.
webhooks.new_url: Copy this URL now. The token is stored only as a digest and cannot be shown again.
webhooks.template_none: — none, send the payload as it came —
people.heading: Installing the bot for everyone
people.explainer: Teamster installs the bot's Teams app for every enabled member of the tenant, so IT can message anyone. A run lists the members, installs the app where it is missing, and runs again every reconcile interval.
people.refresh: A run is in progress — refresh
people.requested: Install run requested. The next check picks it up within 30 seconds.
people.run_counts: {0} listed · {1} installed · {2} already had it · {3} failed · {4} ineligible
notifications.bind_no_account: We could not find your Teams account from how you signed in. Ask an administrator to check the object-id claim, or sign in with your work account.
notifications.bind_no_chat: We found your Teams account, but the bot has no chat with you yet. Set it up now, or wait for the next install run.
notifications.bind_local: You signed in with the local account, which has no Teams chat. Sign in with your work account to receive the alerts routed to you.
notifications.chat_set_up: Your Teams chat is set up. Alerts routed to you arrive there.
notifications.chat_not_ready: The bot could not open a chat with you yet. Try again in a minute, or ask an administrator to check the install.
notifications.setup_failed: Setting up your chat failed. Try again later.
notifications.codes_not_needed: Link codes are not used here: your chat is found from your sign-in.
audit.heading: Configuration changes
audit.explainer: Every change to templates, destinations, routes, webhooks, tokens and permissions, newest first, with what the record held before and after.
audit.no_detail: No fields recorded for this change.
audit.disabled: Nothing is recorded here: set audit.database to true to keep the audit trail in the database.
users.heading: People who have signed in
users.explainer: Everyone who has signed in, with the roles and groups their identity provider sent last time. Disabling someone ends their sessions and refuses their next sign-in. The local login cannot be disabled.
users.empty: Nobody has signed in yet, or nobody matches.
groups.heading: Groups
groups.explainer: A group collects users, other groups and groups your identity provider names at sign-in. Permissions can then be given to the group rather than to each person.
groups.name: Name
